decks.module: Sharing the road with commercial vehicles
decks.domain: Emergency Vehicles, Golf Carts, and Low-Speed Vehicles

cards.front: What should you do when a commercial rig approaches from the other direction?
cards.back: When a commercial rig approaches from the opposite way, hug the right edge so the two vehicles never sideswipe.

cards.front: Why should you never squeeze between a right-turning rig and the curb?
cards.back: Big rigs often swing wide left before a right turn, so never squeeze between the rig and the curb where its driver cannot see you.

cards.front: May you cross behind a commercial vehicle that is backing up?
cards.back: Never cross behind a commercial vehicle that is backing up or about to back up, because its bulk hides everything behind it.

cards.front: What steps come before passing a rig?
cards.back: Before passing a rig, check ahead and behind, enter the passing lane only when it is clear and safe, signal the lane change, and blink your headlights to warn its driver.

cards.front: On which side and how fast should you pass a rig?
cards.back: Pass commercial vehicles on the left for best visibility and finish the pass fast instead of cruising in their blind spots.

cards.front: When may you move back in front of a rig after passing?
cards.back: Never cut back too soon after passing a rig since it brakes slower than cars; wait until you see its cab in your rear-view mirror, and note its driver may flash headlights when merging back is safe.
cards.memory_hook: See the cab in your mirror

cards.front: Should you pass a commercial vehicle on a downgrade?
cards.back: Skip passing a commercial vehicle on a downgrade, where its weight and momentum keep gaining speed.

cards.front: What should you do while a rig passes you?
cards.back: While a commercial vehicle passes you, stay on the right side of your lane and never speed up.

cards.front: How does your side differ when meeting a rig versus passing one?
cards.back: Oncoming rigs demand the right edge while passing a rig demands the left lane, so direction decides the side.

cards.front: What is the gap between a turning rig and the curb?
cards.back: Right-turning rigs swing wide left first, which makes the gap between rig and curb a blind trap rather than an opening.
cards.memory_hook: The curb gap is a trap

cards.front: Why is crossing behind a backing rig banned?
cards.back: A backing rig hides everything behind its bulk, so crossing behind it is banned whether it is moving or only preparing.

cards.front: What are the four moves of a legal rig pass?
cards.back: A legal rig pass chains four moves: check both ways, take the lane only when clear and safe, signal, and blink headlights at its driver.

cards.front: How do you finish a rig pass safely?
cards.back: Finish rig passes fast on the left and merge back only after spotting the cab in your mirror, because lingering in the blind spot or cutting in early both risk a crash.
cards.memory_hook: Pass fast, merge after the cab

cards.front: What rules apply on downgrades and while being passed by a rig?
cards.back: Downgrades forbid passing a rig while being passed by one forbids speeding up, and both cases keep you right.

decks.domain: Emergency Vehicles, Golf Carts, and Low-Speed Vehicles

cards.front: Who must yield to emergency vehicles with sirens or flashing lights?
cards.back: Drivers, bicyclists, and walkers must all yield to police cars, fire engines, and other emergency vehicles running sirens or flashing lights.

cards.front: What do you do when an emergency vehicle approaches?
cards.back: At the approach of an emergency vehicle, pull to the nearest road edge at once and stop until it passes, keeping every intersection clear.

cards.front: How do funeral processions move through intersections?
cards.back: Yield to funeral processions; after the lead car enters an intersection, the rest of the line may follow through no matter what the signals or signs say.

cards.front: How are funeral cars marked, and may you cut into the line?
cards.back: Every car in a funeral line runs headlights or flashing hazard lights, and other drivers must never cut into the procession.

cards.front: What do sirens or flashing lights order road users to do?
cards.back: Sirens or flashing lights from police, fire, or rescue vehicles order every road user to the nearest edge to stop, with intersections left open.

cards.front: When may a funeral line pass signals, and may outsiders break in?
cards.back: A funeral line follows its leader through intersections past any signal once the lead car has entered, and outsiders never break the line.

decks.domain: Emergency Vehicles, Golf Carts, and Low-Speed Vehicles

cards.front: Where may golf carts be driven?
cards.back: Golf carts belong only on golf courses or roadways posted for them with proper signs.

cards.front: What identification must golf cart drivers carry on public roads?
cards.back: Drivers under age eighteen need a valid learner license or driver license to take a cart onto a public road, and drivers eighteen or older must hold valid government-issued photo identification.
cards.memory_hook: Under eighteen: license; over: photo ID

cards.front: May carts run where the county or city has not allowed them?
cards.back: A cart may not run at all in a county or city that has not expressly allowed it.

cards.front: During what hours may carts run?
cards.back: Carts run only between sunrise and sunset unless the local government authorizes night driving with added equipment.

cards.front: Where may a cart cross a state road?
cards.back: A cart may cross a state road only where the posted limit is forty-five miles per hour or less and only at an intersection with a traffic control device.

cards.front: Which sidewalks may carts use?
cards.back: Carts may use a sidewalk at least five feet wide, always yielding to people on foot.

cards.front: Which traffic laws must cart drivers obey?
cards.back: Cart drivers obey every state and local traffic law, including yielding the right-of-way.

cards.front: What equipment must every cart have?
cards.back: Every cart needs efficient brakes, a rear-view mirror, reliable steering, red warning reflectors front and rear, and safe tires.

cards.front: May child passenger seats be used on golf carts?
cards.back: Child passenger seats must stay off golf carts and other low-speed vehicles because they are never crash-tested for them and may fail; follow the seat maker guidance.

cards.front: What does night cart driving require?
cards.back: Night cart driving demands headlights, brake lights, turn signals, and a windshield.

cards.front: Where are carts confined, and what local approval is needed?
cards.back: Carts are confined to courses and sign-posted cart roads, and only where the county or city has affirmatively allowed them.

cards.front: What identification does each age group of cart drivers show?
cards.back: Cart drivers under eighteen show a learner or driver license on public roads while drivers eighteen and up show government photo identification.

cards.front: What are the cart limits on hours, crossings and sidewalks?
cards.back: Carts run sunrise to sunset, cross state roads only at forty-five miles per hour or less through controlled intersections, and take only sidewalks five feet or wider while yielding to walkers.

cards.front: What gear do carts need by day and night, and are child seats allowed?
cards.back: Day carts carry brakes, mirror, steering, red reflectors, and safe tires, night adds headlights, brake lights, signals, and windshield, and child seats are banned from carts entirely.

decks.domain: Emergency Vehicles, Golf Carts, and Low-Speed Vehicles

cards.front: What is a low-speed vehicle, and who may drive one?
cards.back: Low-speed vehicles run on four wheels with top speeds from twenty-one to twenty-five miles per hour, converted carts qualify, and every operator needs a valid driver license.

cards.front: Where may low-speed vehicles go, and what must they carry?
cards.back: Low-speed vehicles stay on streets posted thirty-five miles per hour or less, must carry headlamps, stop lamps, turn signals, tail lamps, reflectors, parking brakes, rear-view mirrors, a windshield, safety belts, and a vehicle identification number, and must be registered and properly insured.

cards.front: What rights and duties do motorcycle and moped riders have?
cards.back: Motorcycle and moped riders keep the same road rights and duties as car drivers and face citations for violations.

cards.front: May a motorist share a lane with a motorcycle?
cards.back: A motorist must never split a lane with a motorcycle, whose rider is entitled to the whole lane.

cards.front: What are the speed, street and equipment limits for low-speed vehicles?
cards.back: Low-speed vehicles top out from twenty-one to twenty-five miles per hour on streets posted thirty-five miles per hour or less with full lights, belts, brakes, mirrors, windshield, VIN, registration, insurance, and a licensed driver.

cards.front: What rights do motorcycles have, and can their lane be shared?
cards.back: Motorcycles and mopeds share car rights and duties plus citation exposure, and no motorist may split their lane since the rider owns it fully.

recaps.module: Sharing the road with commercial vehicles

recap_hooks.text: Hug the right edge for oncoming rigs, never squeeze beside a right-turning rig or cross behind a backing one, and pass on the left quickly, merging back only after you see the cab.
Pull to the nearest edge and stop for sirens or flashing lights, and never cut into a funeral procession.
Golf carts run only on courses and signed roads where locals allow them, between sunrise and sunset, with required equipment and no child seats.
Low-speed vehicles stay on streets posted thirty-five or less with full equipment and a licensed driver, and no one splits a lane with a motorcycle.
